newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy cuts discount rate to 7.5 pct from 8.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Italy cuts discount rate to 7.5 pct from 8.25 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Italy said on Wednesday it would cut the official discount rate to 7.5 percent from 8.25 percent, effective from Thursday.
The last change to the discount rate was on July 23, when it was reduced by 75 basis points.
The Bank's fixed term advances, or Lombard rate, was simultaneously cut to 9.0 percent from a previous 9.75 percent.
The move was certain to be welcomed by Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government, which is keen to see official rates fall to help reduce interest repayments on Italy's huge debt mountain.
A Bank of Italy statement said the reduction reflected falling inflation "towards levels coherent with the aim of inflation of firmly below three percent in 1997".
Preliminary consumer price data issued by 10 Italian cities on Monday and Tuesday pointed to an October inflation rate of 3.0 percent.
